clue.text: American chemical company taken in by staff person on the fiddle perhaps

indicators.note: the letters for the American chemical company are swallowed up by the word for staff

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, the British chemical company

explanation.surface: Someone is employed by an American chemical firm and is on the fiddle, cheating the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the fiddle' suggests fraud, but here it means playing a violin. ICI is Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British chemicals giant.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist is one example of a player of music, hence the 'perhaps' marking an example.

clue.text: Without wishing, fast watch rudely gets stuck around five

indicators.note: the word for staring is pushed around the numeral, holding it inside

parts.note: to stare is to look at someone rudely
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone forced to fast stares rudely at five others eating.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole opening phrase: to go without food not by choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Fasting is voluntary; going hungry against one's will is to be deprived of food.

clue.text: Runs meeting rockers?

explanation.surface: A rock band runs a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rockers' suggests musicians but means rocking seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who presides over a meeting is said to take that role; and rocking seats are furniture of that kind.

clue.text: Scientist whose research needs looking up

definitions.text: Scientist whose research needs looking up

parts.words: Scientist whose research needs looking up
parts.note: looking up reads as consulting reference books, but literally means gazing at the sky

explanation.surface: A scientist whose work needs checking in the library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking up' seems to mean looking things up in references; the scientist literally looks upward at the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A student of stars and planets spends research time gazing skywards through telescopes.

clue.text: House's top storey left out, contrarily

indicators.note: going the contrary way, the remaining letters are read from back to front
the letter for left is dropped from the word for a storey

parts.note: a storey of a building is a floor

explanation.surface: An architect's note: the top storey of the house has been left out, against expectations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes L from FLOOR, leaving FOOR, and 'contrarily' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The covering on the very top of a house is its roof, so 'house's top' is a plain description.

clue.text: First to get over splintered railing

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

indicators.note: a splintered railing is broken into pieces, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A splintered railing gets knocked over first.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest version of something, from which copies are made, is the first.

clue.text: UK ministry, talking shop with its counterparts, will meet volunteers in spring

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, a British government department
the UN is where the UK talks with other countries, often mocked as a talking shop
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A government department talks with its counterparts and meets volunteers in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a water source. The Territorial Army (TA) is the UK's part-time volunteer military reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a natural source of water, as is a jet of water rising from the ground.

clue.text: Cultivating grass in Crosby?

indicators.note: the grass word sits inside the singer's first name

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the American crooner
a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: Bing Crosby, perhaps, growing grass on his lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Bing Crosby was an American singer and actor, so 'Crosby' gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising plants or animals to develop new varieties is a way of cultivating them.

clue.text: People farming small-scale little vegetables and animals

parts.note: peas are small green vegetables
ants are tiny creatures, counted as animals here

explanation.surface: A smallholding picture: small farmers growing baby vegetables and keeping livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animals' sounds like farm livestock but is just insects, ANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Peasants are traditionally rural folk who work a small plot of land for their living.

clue.text: Section of biography perhaps shows anger when sacrificing rook for pawn

indicators.note: as in chess, one piece is given up and another put in its place

parts.note: rage is fierce anger
R is the chess notation for rook
P is the chess notation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess player's biography shows anger at sacrificing a rook for a pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the replacement: R in RAGE is swapped for P.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf of any book, a biography for instance, is one section of the text.

clue.text: It's not very long and very small

definitions.meaning: a short space of time, sixty seconds

explanation.surface: A modest description of something short and tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt alike but said differently: MIN-it for the time and my-NEWT for the size.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixty seconds is a brief stretch of time, and as an adjective the word means tiny.

clue.text: Grand bit of cricket attended by neither head of state?

parts.note: G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand pounds
an over is a set of six balls in cricket
the word nor pairs with neither

explanation.surface: A grand cricket match attended by no head of state at all.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six balls from one bowler. 'neither' supplies NOR as its partner word in 'neither ... nor'.
explanation.definitionFit: In US states and many colonies the elected chief executive of the state carries this title.

clue.text: Fifty diets represented on the menu?

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: the letters of diets are presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: A restaurant shows fifty different diets on its menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' is read as re-presented, rearranging DIETS to ISTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything printed on a menu has been entered in a written list, the question mark marking the playful sense.

clue.text: What's needed for 1 part of refrain — strum enthusiastically!

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Instructions for a song: the refrain should be strummed enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition stopped at 'What's needed', leaving 'for 1' as a link; the definition needs 'for 1', the cross-reference to 1 Across, a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician (1 Across) needs something to play, such as a guitar or violin.

clue.text: Discovered one in a hundred will offer charity, say

parts.note: to have discovered something is to have found it

indicators.note: the numeral for one goes inside the letters for a hundred

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that one in a hundred people will give to charity.
explanation.walkthrough: TON is British slang for a hundred (pounds, or miles per hour).
explanation.definitionFit: A charitable trust or endowed institution is often called by this name, so a charity is one example.

clue.text: Putting coat on, yearns for old-fashioned measurements

indicators.note: in a down clue the coat is placed on top, above the next piece

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur
to yearn is to long for something

explanation.surface: Someone putting on a coat yearns for the old-fashioned way of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: A furlong is an eighth of a mile, still used in British horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: These eighth-of-a-mile lengths are imperial units, now mostly confined to horse racing.

clue.text: Dead drunk, imbibing barely changed

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the next piece as a drinker takes in drink
drunk letters reel about into a new order

parts.note: just means barely, only just

explanation.surface: A dead-drunk drinker, imbibing still, barely changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead drunk' reads as one phrase, but 'drunk' is the anagram signal giving ADED, and 'imbibing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To have altered or tweaked something slightly is to have modified it.

clue.text: Cyber bullies set about the old over moving beds?

indicators.note: the word for online bullies is set around the next piece

parts.note: trolls post abuse online

indicators.note: in a down clue over says the archaic word is turned upside down

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: Online trolls attack the elderly, who are moved about in hospital beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' flips the archaic word to EY in this down clue, and 'set about' wraps the bullies round it; the question mark flags beds on wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital patients are wheeled about on wheeled stretchers, beds that move.

clue.text: The nude ran, wobbling below

indicators.note: the wobbling letters of the three words are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A streaker runs naked, everything wobbling as they go.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying lower than something else is to be beneath it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Secure in wrecked boat at first

indicators.note: the anagram comes first, before the little word
a wrecked boat is broken up, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Something made safe inside a wrecked boat at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure a thing is to get hold of it, acquire it.

clue.text: Hip and excellent island state

parts.note: hips and haws are both red hedgerow fruits, taken as equivalent here
A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A hip and excellent island state, a fashionable holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip and excellent island' looks like a description of the state; only 'state' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific archipelago is the fiftieth member of the United States.

clue.text: Going up, for instance, from French border

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom

parts.note: EG stands for exempli gratia, for instance
de is French for from

explanation.surface: Climbing, for example, from the French border.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is the rim or margin of something, its outer limit.

clue.text: Resoundingly haughty king's dropped out, university's admitted

indicators.note: the university letter is let into the gap left behind
the letter for king falls out of the word for haughty

parts.note: lordly means arrogant and haughty
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A haughty king loudly drops out, and a university lets someone in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped out' removes R from LORDLY, leaving LODLY, and 'admitted' puts U in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that resounds is very noisy, so to act resoundingly is to do it with great volume.

clue.text: Cabinet's award going to 'Shakespeare in Love'? On the contrary

parts.note: a cup is a trophy given as an award

indicators.note: together with the reversal instruction this places love inside the poet, not the other way round
the clue says Shakespeare goes in love; contrary to that, love goes in Shakespeare

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare's nickname
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: The film Shakespeare in Love wins an award, here a cabinet's prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'Shakespeare in Love' to love in Shakespeare: O inside BARD gives BOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet is a piece of furniture with shelves and doors, the same as a cupboard.

clue.text: Trapped in poverty, having to keep dry

indicators.note: the word for poverty holds the letters for dry inside it

parts.note: need means poverty or want
TT, teetotal, describes someone who keeps off drink

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in poverty has to stay off alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: TT means teetotal, so 'dry' in the no-alcohol sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught in a net, as a fish or a goal is, means trapped.

clue.text: Guided westwards, with sensitive state of the east

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means reading right to left

parts.note: to have guided someone is to have led them
being sensitive to something is being aware of it

explanation.surface: Someone was guided westwards with care, sensitive to the eastern state.
explanation.definitionFit: This US state lies on the Atlantic seaboard, so it is a state of the eastern United States.

clue.text: Sky can be seen through this bit of pottery?

definitions.text: Sky can be seen through this
definitions.meaning: a satellite receiver for the Sky television service
a plate or bowl, an item of crockery

explanation.surface: A cracked pot so broken you can see the sky through it.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster, received by a satellite dish on the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite receiver bowl and a serving bowl share this name.

clue.text: Crooning about tango is creating irritation

indicators.note: the singing word goes about the letter for tango, enclosing it

parts.note: crooning is a soft kind of singing
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone crooning a tango is getting on everyone's nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: A nettle's smarting effect irritates the skin, as does a sharp remark.
